markdownDescription:
## Ad Funnel Studio

A product photo and a campaign brief become a five-frame campaign — hero, problem, solution, proof, call to action — one look, one series, ready to run as a sequence. The product stays exactly as photographed, and the last frame also comes out as a video: the ad building itself piece by piece.

1. **Product photo** — a clean packshot. The hero of every frame.
2. **Campaign brief** — who you are, who you sell to, the problem, the proof you can stand behind, the offer.
3. **Moodboard** — optional. One picture of your brand world.
4. **Campaign strategy** — an AI strategist writes the insight, the promise, the tone, the look, and one line per frame.
5. **Five frames** — one writer per frame, each feeding its own ad, all in the strategy's look. Edit a brief by hand and rerun just its ad.
6. **The CTA in motion** — the call-to-action frame becomes an 8-second entrance clip: empty background, then every element arrives. Wire any other frame into Ad Motion Studio for the same.

data.text: Business: ARDEN — a small audio house. Product: ARDEN Solace — wireless over-ear headphones with active noise cancelling, deep burgundy leather cushions, brushed brass details and a 40-hour battery. Customer: 30 to 50, commuters and open-plan office workers who want quiet and are tired of tech that looks like gym equipment. Problem it solves: the office and the train never go quiet, and most noise-cancelling headphones are plastic and loud-looking. Proof we can stand behind: in our own lab the noise cancelling removes up to 40 dB of low-frequency noise; in our two-week trial 9 of 10 testers said they focused better. Offer: a leather travel case free with every launch order. Tone: calm, confident, a little wry.

Campaign strategy
data.userInput: Campaign brief: {Campaign brief || a premium consumer product for a design-minded audience.} The reference images are the product photo and, if present, the brand moodboard. Write the strategy.
data.systemPrompt:
You are a direct-response strategist for consumer brands. From the campaign brief, the product photo and the moodboard if there is one, write the campaign strategy in exactly this shape, plain English, nothing else:
Insight: <one sentence — the customer truth the campaign stands on>
Promise: <one sentence — what the product does for them>
Tone: <a few words>
Look: <one paragraph of 50 to 80 words: background colours and finish, typography feel, how the product is shown, light, mood — one look every frame follows>
Hero: <one sentence — what the attention frame says>
Problem: <one sentence — the frustration the customer knows>
Solution: <one sentence — how the product fixes it, with the one ingredient or mechanism from the brief>
Proof: <one sentence — the evidence the brief gives, quoted faithfully; if the brief gives none, write: none>
CTA: <one sentence — the offer and the action from the brief>
Use only facts the brief states; never invent studies, numbers or ingredients. No other headings, no commentary.

data.label: Ad breakdown
data.userInput: Describe the advertisement in the reference image.
data.systemPrompt: You describe finished advertisements for an image editor and a motion designer. Look at the reference image and write ONE paragraph of plain English, 80 to 130 words, in this order: first the background alone (its colours, gradient, light, texture, and where the light comes from); then every element that sits on it, back to front, one short sentence each, naming what it is, where it sits and its colours, and quoting any text on it word for word in double quotes; finish with one sentence that begins with the words Remove everything except the background and lists the elements to remove. Only what is visible. No opinions, no bullet points, no headings, no commentary. Output only the paragraph.

data.label: Clean background
data.prompt: Recreate the reference advertisement exactly — same size, same framing, same background colours, gradient, light and texture — but with every element removed, leaving only the empty background: no text, no headline, no logo, no product, no badge, no button, no decorative object, and no shadow or reflection of anything removed. Fill every gap so the background reads as one continuous, untouched surface with the same light. What is on the ad: {Ad breakdown || the background and every element on it.} Output only the empty background with nothing on it.

data.label: Entrance director
data.userInput: The elements on the ad, back to front: {Ad breakdown || see the finished ad.} Of the two reference images, the one with nothing on it is the first frame (the empty background) and the complete advertisement is the last frame. Write the entrance.
data.systemPrompt: You are a senior motion designer writing the prompt for a video model that is given a first frame and a last frame. The first frame is the empty background of an advertisement; the last frame is the finished advertisement. Write ONE paragraph of 110 to 160 words that builds the finished ad on the empty background piece by piece over 8 seconds: a touch of light first, then the product fading in where it stands with its shadow, then the supporting graphics, then the headline, then the smaller text, then the button, then a final settling micro-motion. The last second holds perfectly still on the finished advertisement with every element exactly in its final place. Name each element by what it is and quote its exact text. For each one say how it arrives, how it eases, and roughly when it settles, so the whole sequence fills the 8 seconds with staggered motion rather than everything at once. Every element arrives in its own final place — fading in, wiping in, or sliding no more than a finger's width — and nothing ever enters from beyond the edge of the frame or crosses the frame, so no element is ever seen twice. The product never rises from below the frame and never slides in from a side: it fades in where it stands, shadow and reflection with it. Text and logos arrive by sliding, wiping or fading in — never by scaling up from nothing, which smears the letters. Keep the camera almost still — at most one slow, subtle push. Do not crossfade, do not redraw or reinterpret anything, and never change any text, logo or product. Plain English, present tense, no headings, no lists, no timestamps in brackets, no quotation marks around the paragraph. Output only the paragraph.

data.label: CTA · Entrance
data.prompt: {Entrance director || The elements of the advertisement arrive one by one on the empty background — the product first, then the graphics, the headline, the smaller text and the button — each easing into its final place while the camera stays almost still, ending exactly on the finished advertisement.} Crisp, stable motion-graphics animation; every element appears once, in its final place, and nothing enters from beyond the edges of the frame; text, logo and product stay exactly as designed; no duplicates, no morphing, no flicker, no extra objects, no camera shake, no scene change.
